newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada grain co-ops bid for United Grain.
newsitem.headline: Canada grain co-ops bid for United Grain.

text.p: Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators said on Thursday that they will make a C$13.75 per share offer for all shares in United Grain Growers Ltd.

The grain handling co-operatives already own 15 percent of UUG's shares through a jointly owned private holding company. The company has entered into a lock-up agreement to buy another 6.4 percent of UGG's shares, the co-operatives said in a statement.

"The proposed purchase of UGG is driven by (Alberta Wheat Pool's) and (Manitoba Pool's) goal to be stronger, long-term players in an increasingly competitive, less regulated and global industry," the statement said.

The offer, which expires on March 27, is conditional upon the removal of UGG's shareholder rights plan, or so-called poison pill. The rights plan was adopted by UGG's board of directors on February 14. The wheat pools said the C$13.75 a share offer represents a 34 percent premium to the C$10.23 average closing price of UGG's stock before the pools began buying UGG shares in January.
The pools estimated the total value of the bid at C$172 million, not including acquisition and integration costs.

"This acquisition will ensure that UGG's substantial assets are not acquired by foreign competitors and as such, it presents a defensive benefit for (Alberta Wheat Pool) and (Manitoba Pool) and their members," the statement said.

Winnipeg-based UGG is Canada's third-largest grain handling company, behind number two, Alberta Wheat Pool, and number one, Saskatchewan Wheat Pool. UGG operates 173 elevator facilities in Western Canada, two terminals in Thunder Bay, Ontario and one terminal in Vancouver, British Columbia.
UGG also owns a 16.3 percent interest in a terminal in Prince Rupert, British Columbia.

UGG made history in 1992 when it became the first Canadian grain co-operative to offer shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Saskatchewan Wheat Pool followed UGG onto Canada's largest stock market last year.

Following the acquisition, the pools said they will continue to operate as co-operatives in their respective provinces. The pools also plan to form a new, joint venture co-operative to serve Saskatchewan farmers.
